subject: MAP reconvene — procurement hold & phased close options
messages:
From: Darren Brooks <darren.brooks@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: procurement hold affecting MAP dates

Irene,

Quick note — procurement just flagged a new security addendum request this morning and put a temporary hold on all signature approvals. The net effect is that our signed PO timeline will slip by ~2–3 weeks.

We still want to move forward with Redwood but need to understand options on your side. Two asks from our procurement team:
- Can we pause the current MAP evaluation gate dates formally so we don’t trigger internal SLAs?
- Alternatively, can we run a limited phased go-live (sandbox -> limited production) while paperwork catches up?

Attaching the procurement hold notice for your records. Let me know what flexibility is available and any implications for pricing or scheduling.

Thanks,
Darren Brooks
Senior Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp
[attachment: procurement_hold_notice.pdf (PDF)]
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Darren Brooks <darren.brooks@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: procurement hold affecting MAP dates

Hi Darren — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the notice. Sorry to hear procurement is adding an extra review. We can accommodate both patterns but want to be explicit about tradeoffs so your teams can pick the least risky path. Options we recommend:

1) Rebaseline MAP (recommended if paperwork will take >10 business days)
   - Move evaluation gate and final go-live by +3 weeks (we’ll preserve test criteria)
   - No change to unit pricing, but we require a written MAP amendment to lock milestones

2) Phased go-live (recommended if procurement delay is short)
   - Limited production with a throughput cap and data partitioning for the pilot
   - Temporary credit on overage charges during pilot; full commercial terms apply on final cutover

3) Short pilot extension / credit (if you need to leave map dates but need runway)
   - 30-day extension on evaluation window + one-time 10% credit on pilot invoices

Next steps: please confirm which option procurement prefers and share a single point of contact at procurement for the MAP amendment (we’ll draft a one‑page change order). If you like, we can also convene a 30‑minute reconvene meeting this week to align stakeholders.

I’ll loop in our cross-functional owners once you confirm.

— Irene Choi
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: procurement hold affecting MAP dates

Forwarding Darren's note — procurement hold looks like 2–3 weeks. Thoughts on concessions and escalation?

My read: we should offer a clear, low-effort path that keeps the deal moving and reduces churn risk. Proposed internal position:
- Approve option 1 (formal MAP rebaseline) as default: shift milestones + preserve pricing.
- If Acme asks for partial production before signature, allow phased go-live with:
  * throughput cap (we will size capacity for pilot)
  * temporary 10% credit on pilot billing during hold
  * requirement: signed one‑page amendment (no change to long-term T&C)
- If delay goes beyond 21 days, escalate to sales leadership for additional concessions (discounts / extended credits).

Marissa — can you prep a 1‑page MAP amendment template (xlsx) we can send if Darren picks rebaseline? Markus — confirm we can technically enforce a throughput cap and data partitioning on Dedicated pools.

Thanks Irene — that all sounds reasonable. Procurement is open to option 2 (phased go-live) provided we have:
- An updated MAP with the new go-live milestones and an explicit note about pilot throughput caps
- A short invoice pause clause while the PO is being finalized (procurement requires this in writing)

I'll attach the procurement form they asked us to fill out. Can you send a short MAP amendment and the proposed pilot credit number? We aim to reconvene engineering and procurement on Friday.

Attached: procurement_form_acme_v2.pdf

— Darren
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: MAP amendment & next steps (ACME-4721)

Quick summary / actions from the last 48 hours:
- Acme chooses phased go‑live. They requested an updated MAP with: pilot milestone, throughput cap, and invoice pause line.
- Darren submitted procurement_form_acme_v2.pdf (attached in thread).
- Internal ask: Marissa to send proposed_map_rebaseline.xlsx (1‑page amendment) to Darren with a temporary 10% pilot credit and invoice pause language.
- Markus to confirm capacity gating and provide operational notes for the MAP amendment.

If procurement pushes beyond 21 calendar days we escalate to Rishi for discretionary concessions (we will not unilaterally exceed the 10% pilot credit without leadership approval). I've added the deal to our risk tracker and created the HubSpot note here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-4721
